mechanism_narrative: A rising CPIAUCSL (consumer price index) in the prior month signals persistent inflation, which is associated with strong economic growth and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days due to the market's anticipation of continued economic expansion and delayed monetary tightening.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when CPIAUCSL increases by at least 0.2% in the prior month (as measured by the monthly change), as tested by a t-test (p>0.05) over the 2005-2024 period.

mechanism_narrative: A FEDFUNDS rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to the market's immediate reaction to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, as tested by a t-test (p>0.05) over the 2005-2024 period.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in INDPRO (industrial production) coupled with a rise in UNRATE (unemployment rate) signals a weakening economy with deteriorating labor market conditions, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to the market's anticipation of reduced corporate earnings and potential recession.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO decreases by at least 0.5% and UNRATE increases by at least 0.2% in the prior month (as measured by the monthly change), as tested by a t-test (p>0.05) over the 2005-2024 period.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising HOUST (housing starts) and rising RSAFS (residential fixed investment) signals a late-cycle expansion, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days (one quarter) due to the market's anticipation of monetary tightening and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both HOUST and RSAFS increase by at least 0.5% in the prior month (as measured by the monthly change), as tested by a t-test (p>0.05) over the 2005-2024 period.

mechanism_narrative: A UNRATE below 4.5% signals a tight labor market, which is associated with strong consumer spending and positive equity returns over the next 5 trading days due to the market's anticipation of continued economic expansion and delayed monetary tightening.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE is below 4.5%, as tested by a t-test (p>0.05) over the 2005-2024 period.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising HOUST (housing starts) and rising CPIAUCSL (inflation) signals a strong economy with persistent inflation, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days (one quarter) as the market prices in continued economic expansion and delayed monetary tightening.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and CPIAUCSL increase by at least 0.5% in the prior month (as measured by the monthly change), as tested by a t-test (p>0.05) over the 2005-2024 period.

mechanism_narrative: A rising PAYEMS (non-farm payrolls) signals strong labor market conditions, which are associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days (one quarter) due to the market's anticipation of continued economic expansion and delayed monetary tightening.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.2% in the prior month (as measured by the monthly change), as tested by a t-test (p>0.05) over the 2005-2024 period.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL annual inflation rate above 2.0% signals persistent inflation, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to the market's anticipation of continued economic expansion and delayed monetary tightening.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the annual change in CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.0%, as tested by a t-test (p>0.05) over the 2005-2024 period.
